title: M4ri Public Matrix V1
objective: Make public dense GF(2) matrices canonically own generated M4RI resources when available, preserve packed fallback and explicit alternate backends, and verify direct algebra, lifecycle, serialization, formatting, and typed-Python borrowing without hidden exports

exceptions: Public ordinary Python matrix semantics combine generated M4RI external resources with one source-transparent typed-Python borrowing witness

handoff.summary: Dense GF(2) matrices now canonically own generated M4RI resources where the capability is available. Construction, access, mutation, copying, arithmetic, structural algorithms, formatting, serialization, and lifecycle stay on the resource path; explicit FLINT/FFLAS/modp selections remain available through a compatibility export. Three compiled typed-Python kernels safely borrow M4RI matrices for traversal without exporting packed data.
risks: The Windows capability fallback remains the existing packed dense-prime implementation.
Public-path browser execution should be covered by the integration lane even though the generated M4RI Wasm package itself is already tested.
next_steps: Integrate this commit onto dense-qq-resources and run the root portable/browser matrix suite.
Migrate explicit alternative GF(2) algorithm paths to resource-to-resource adapters if eliminating their compatibility exports becomes worthwhile.
